clue.text: Youngster with brave potentialities

definitions.text: Youngster with brave potentialities

parts.words: Youngster with brave potentialities
parts.note: a brave is a young Native American warrior, so this is a baby who may grow into one

explanation.surface: A promising young person with the makings of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective meaning courageous, but here it is the noun for a Native American warrior; the youngster is a baby carried on its mother's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American infant could grow up to be a warrior, a brave in waiting.

clue.text: It's colourful, and suits swineherds to a T

definitions.text: It's colourful

parts.words: swineherds
parts.note: people who tend swine are pig men

parts.words: T

explanation.surface: Something bright that fits pig farmers perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a T' is the idiom for 'exactly', but here the swineherds are joined to a letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour to paint or tissue.

clue.text: Partlet prepared as a dish

definitions.text: a dish

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made ready, so the letters of the hen's name are reworked

parts.words: Partlet

explanation.surface: Partlet, the hen of fable, is cooked and served up.
explanation.walkthrough: Partlet is the traditional name of a hen (Chaucer's Pertelote), which makes 'prepared as a dish' sound like cooking her.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat serving plate is called a platter, as is the food served on it.

clue.text: Arch appeal for a contribution

definitions.text: Arch

parts.words: appeal
parts.note: O is the exclamation that opens a plea or entreaty

parts.words: for a contribution
parts.note: a request for a contribution is the plea 'give'

explanation.surface: A cheeky plea for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks like an adjective meaning roguish, but it is the noun: a pointed Gothic arch or rib.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a pointed arch or diagonal vault rib is known by this term.

clue.text: Little creatures whose head coverings seem to have slipped a bit !

definitions.text: Little creatures whose head coverings seem to have slipped a bit !

parts.words: Little creatures whose head coverings seem to have slipped a bit
parts.note: the insect's name splits as wigs worn over the ears, as if a hairpiece had slid down the side of the head

explanation.surface: Small animals with dishevelled headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the insect's name in two and the head coverings appear, perched lower than usual on the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small pincered insects, the creatures the clue describes.

clue.text: No doubt they can tell tall stories

definitions.text: No doubt they can tell tall stories

parts.words: No doubt they can tell tall stories
parts.note: the stories are the floors of a tall building, which these operators announce as they go up

explanation.surface: People who are good at telling exaggerated tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall stories' suggests fibs, but here the stories are floors of a high building, called out by the attendants who run the elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators of an elevator, called a lift in Britain, call out each floor.

clue.text: Result of strokes of luck rather than of the bat

definitions.text: Result of strokes of luck rather than of the bat

parts.words: Result of strokes of luck rather than of the bat
parts.note: in cricket, runs scored when the ball glances off the batsman's body rather than the bat are recorded separately

explanation.surface: Success through good fortune rather than skill.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg byes are runs taken after the ball hits the batsman's body, not the bat, so they are scored by luck rather than a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: These cricket extras come from the ball deflecting off the batsman's pads or body, not the bat.

clue.text: They're singularly dotty, but have capital followings

definitions.text: They're singularly dotty, but have capital followings

parts.words: They're singularly dotty, but have capital followings
parts.note: each of these punctuation marks is a single dot, and the next sentence begins with a capital letter

explanation.surface: Eccentric people who nonetheless have excellent fan bases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like 'crazy' and 'capital' like 'splendid', but each mark is one dot and is followed by a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These marks end a sentence, so the next word starts with an upper-case letter.

clue.text: Tiny cause of much ill-feeling

definitions.text: Tiny cause of much ill-feeling

parts.words: Tiny cause of much ill-feeling
parts.note: the ill feeling is physical sickness, caused by a minute organism

explanation.surface: A small thing that sparks great resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' suggests resentment, but here it is literally feeling ill, caused by a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ or bacterium is a minute organism that can bring on disease.

clue.text: They might make a family feel the pinch

definitions.text: They might make a family feel the pinch

parts.words: They might make a family feel the pinch
parts.note: small children strain a family's budget, and pincers or pliers literally pinch

explanation.surface: Things that cause a household money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both young children, who strain the family purse, and pincers, which nip.
explanation.definitionFit: Kids in British slang, who cost money, share the name with claws or pincers that squeeze.

clue.text: This artisan would be less diligent if he didn't keep his head

definitions.text: This artisan would be less diligent if he didn't keep his head

parts.words: This artisan would be less diligent if he didn't keep his head
parts.note: remove the first letter of the craftsman's title and what remains is a word meaning less diligent, more idle

explanation.surface: A craftsman who works hard only by staying calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep his head' sounds like staying composed, but it means keeping his first letter: without its G the trade becomes LAZIER.
explanation.definitionFit: This craftsman fits panes into windows, a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Suitable reward for a sterling performance?

definitions.text: Suitable reward for a sterling performance?

parts.words: Suitable reward for a sterling performance
parts.note: sterling suggests precious metal, and a race trophy made of it rewards the winner

explanation.surface: A fitting prize for an excellent show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sterling' means excellent here on the surface, but hints at precious metal; the Gold Cup is a famous horse-racing trophy, notably at Cheltenham and Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy of precious metal awarded to the winner of a top race.

clue.text: Here's a tip for you

definitions.text: Here's a tip for you

parts.words: Here's a tip for you
parts.note: a tip here is the very end or point of something, not advice or a gratuity

explanation.surface: Someone offering a helpful hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice or a gratuity, but it is the outermost point of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthest end or point of a thing, such as a fingertip.

clue.text: Town where 15 should feel at home

definitions.text: Town where 15 should feel at home

parts.words: Town where 15 should feel at home
parts.note: the town's name is the verb for feeding a furnace, so the furnace workers of the other clue belong there

explanation.surface: A place where a certain group of people would fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke-on-Trent is a Staffordshire pottery town; its name is also the verb for tending a fire, the trade of the people in the cross-referenced clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This English town, in full Stoke-on-Trent, is a Staffordshire pottery centre.

clue.text: Artists in their craft?

definitions.text: Artists in their craft?

parts.words: Artists in their craft
parts.note: lathe workers shape wood skilfully, and J.M.W. Turner was a famous painter

explanation.surface: Masters of their particular trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter J.M.W. Turner hints at artists, but the craft is shaping wood or metal on a lathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lathe workers are craftsmen who shape material by spinning it, and Turner is a painter's name.

clue.text: It's presumably for joint occupation

definitions.text: It's presumably for joint occupation

parts.words: It's presumably for joint occupation
parts.note: the joint is the arm's hinge, and this space lets it move freely

explanation.surface: A property intended to be shared by several people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint occupation' sounds like shared tenancy, but the joint is the elbow, which needs space to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Space to move freely, as if enough to stretch out one's arms.

clue.text: The men in the firing line?

definitions.text: The men in the firing line?

parts.words: The men in the firing line
parts.note: firing here means feeding a furnace, as on a steamship or locomotive

explanation.surface: Soldiers facing the enemy's guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing line' suggests soldiers in battle, but the firing is fuelling a boiler fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who shovel coal into a furnace keep the fire going.

clue.text: In his business, a good turnover is expected

definitions.text: In his business, a good turnover is expected

parts.words: In his business, a good turnover is expected
parts.note: turnover is a somersault or flip, not the volume of trade

explanation.surface: A trader who expects healthy sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like a commercial term, but this performer literally turns over in somersaults.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus tumbler performs flips and somersaults for a living.

clue.text: Walk in which Ada goes about hobbling

definitions.text: Walk

indicators.note: the name goes round the outside of the other word, enclosing it

parts.words: Ada
hobbling
parts.note: someone hobbling is lame

explanation.surface: A path where a woman called Ada walks with a limp.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain and the Americas, a tree-lined public promenade.

clue.text: He did certain dirty work for a sovereign

definitions.text: He did certain dirty work for a sovereign

parts.words: He did certain dirty work for a sovereign
parts.note: legend says this courtier spread his cloak over a muddy puddle for Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A henchman doing a monarch's shady business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty work' suggests villainy, but the story is of Sir Walter laying his cloak in the mud for Queen Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter, Elizabethan courtier and explorer, famed for the cloak and puddle legend.

clue.text: Travellers' requisites

definitions.text: Travellers' requisites

parts.words: Travellers' requisites
parts.note: what a passenger needs to board a train or bus

explanation.surface: Things a traveller must pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Passes or permits for a journey, needed by passengers.

clue.text: It was issued for light service

definitions.text: It was issued for light service

parts.words: It was issued for light service
parts.note: lighting by gas was paid for on a utility account

explanation.surface: Something issued for a minor duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light service' sounds like easy duty, but it is gas lighting, billed by the supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice from the utility that supplied fuel for lamps.

clue.text: One is always going to say it

definitions.text: One is always going to say it

parts.words: One is always going to say it
parts.note: going here means departing, and this is the farewell said on leaving

explanation.surface: Something one is bound to say eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Always going to' looks like 'certain to', but it means someone on the point of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The parting word said when leaving, a farewell.

clue.text: Nice tax adjustment, but not quite correct

definitions.text: not quite correct

indicators.note: an adjustment alters something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.words: Nice tax

explanation.surface: A tax tweak that is slightly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise, falling short of accuracy.

clue.text: In this a draw may be a win

definitions.text: In this a draw may be a win

parts.words: In this a draw may be a win
parts.note: the draw is the picking of tickets, not a tied game

explanation.surface: A contest where tying counts as winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a tied match, but here it is the drawing of numbers, which may win a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chance where prizes go to tickets picked at random.

clue.text: State of the people of Flushing?

definitions.text: State of the people of Flushing?

parts.words: State of the people of Flushing
parts.note: Flushing is a Dutch port, but here people who are flushing are blushing and glowing red

explanation.surface: A question about the citizens of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Flushing (Vlissingen) is a Dutch port, so the capital disguises people who are flushing, red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing warmly, as a red face does when blushing.

clue.text: The highest point to which a sailor may aspire?

definitions.text: The highest point to which a sailor may aspire?

parts.words: The highest point to which a sailor may aspire
parts.note: aspire is taken literally as climbing, to the lookout platform at the top of a mast

explanation.surface: The pinnacle of a seaman's career ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspire' suggests career ambition, but this is the lookout post at the masthead, the highest place a sailor can climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout platform high on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Not the girl who can't say No !

definitions.text: the girl

indicators.note: cant means to tilt or set at an angle, so the words are knocked askew into a new order

parts.words: say No

explanation.surface: Not the girl who always agrees to everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't say no' describes an obliging girl, but 'can't' (cant, tilt) rearranges SAY NO into a Russian girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian female name, the diminutive of Sofia.

clue.text: Is seen in a kind of poem as an interesting happening

definitions.text: an interesting happening

indicators.note: something seen in a thing appears inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.words: a kind of poem
parts.note: an epode is a lyric poem form, as written by Horace

parts.words: Is

explanation.surface: Something appearing in verse as a notable event.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident or event standing out in a sequence.

clue.text: Strip for the doctor?

definitions.text: Strip for the doctor?

parts.words: Strip for the doctor
parts.note: strip is a length of dressing material, not undressing for an examination

explanation.surface: Undressing for a medical examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like the verb to undress, but it is a noun: a strip of dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of fabric used to wrap a wound.

clue.text: It would be a shame to break up these functions

definitions.text: It would be a shame to break up these functions

parts.words: It would be a shame to break up these functions
parts.note: functions are social receptions held in one's house, and to break up is to end the party

explanation.surface: Gatherings that ought not to be ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Functions' could be roles or purposes, but they are informal receptions given at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal receptions held in a private house.

clue.text: Suitable sub-title for Kipling's " Just-So Stories "?

definitions.text: Suitable sub-title for Kipling's " Just-So Stories "?

parts.words: Suitable sub-title for Kipling's " Just-So Stories "
parts.note: the phrase just so means precisely, so a subtitle could restate it

explanation.surface: A proposed alternative title for a classic children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories explain how animals came to be; 'just so' also means precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Precisely, the sense of the phrase just so.
